articles.title: Highly frequent undesired insertional mutagenesis during Drosophila genome editing
articles.summary: CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing utilizes Homology Directed Repair (HDR) from template vector sequences to achieve precise genetic modifications. This widely used technique enables scientists to make targeted insertions, deletions, or alterations within an organism's DNA. It's a fundamental tool in biotechnology, crucial for advanced research in genetics and holds significant promise for future therapeutic applications and understanding biological processes.

articles.title: Australia fires new defence system designed to intercept rockets as outrage grows over China's missile test in the South Pacific
articles.summary: The Australian Defence Force released footage of its ground-based air defence system testing, occurring days after China tested an intercontinental ballistic missile in the South Pacific. It signals readiness and a focus on counter-measures amidst evolving military developments and geopolitical challenges in the Indo-Pacific.

articles.title: Furious Putin rounded on his advisers for suggesting a ceasefire - and plans to escalate the war within weeks, Kremlin sources tell Reuters
articles.summary: Kremlin sources indicate President Putin seeks to escalate the war in Ukraine, reportedly turning on advisers who advocated for peace negotiations with Kyiv. This development suggests a hardening stance from Russia, moving away from diplomatic solutions despite internal recommendations. The move could significantly impact the conflict's future trajectory and international stability, demanding close observation.

articles.title: “The Pitt”, “Hacks”, “Widow’s Bay” Dominate 2026 Emmy Nominations
articles.summary: The 2026 Emmy nominations have been announced, recognizing excellence in television. 'The Pitt' leads the race with an impressive 25 nominations. Comedy series 'Hacks' made history, securing 24 nominations, a new record for its genre in a single year. 'Widow’s Bay' also garnered significant recognition, being among the top contenders for the prestigious awards.

articles.title: Tata, Nibe likely to bag Indian Army's ₹1,600 crore loitering munition tender
articles.summary: Indian firms Tata Advanced Systems and Nibe Limited are the lowest bidders for the Indian Army's tender to acquire 840 advanced loitering munitions. Valued at approximately ₹1,600 crore, these drones with a 100 Km range will significantly enhance the Army's precision strike capabilities. This procurement underscores India's focus on modernizing its arsenal and boosting indigenous defence manufacturing for strategic self-reliance.
